holidays.name: International Day of Happiness
holidays.description: A global day dedicated to recognizing that happiness is a fundamental human goal. People celebrate with acts of kindness, smile-a-thons, and generally trying to be less grumpy than usual.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly established it in 2012, following a proposal led by Bhutan, the country famous for measuring Gross National Happiness instead of just GDP.
holidays.funFact: Bhutan's king introduced the concept of Gross National Happiness in the 1970s, valuing citizens' well-being over economic output.

holidays.name: World Sparrow Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the humble house sparrow, a tiny bird that has quietly shared our cities for thousands of years and is now declining in many places. Fans celebrate by putting out birdseed, water, and nest boxes.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2010 by the Nature Forever Society of India, with the Eco-Sys Action Foundation in France and other groups, to raise awareness of declining urban sparrow populations.
holidays.funFact: House sparrows have lived alongside humans since the dawn of agriculture and are found on nearly every continent, yet their numbers have dropped sharply in parts of Europe and Asia.

holidays.name: Great American Meatout
holidays.description: A day when people are encouraged to try a vegetarian or vegan diet for 24 hours. It is the carnivore's chance to say 'hold the steak' and see what a plate of vegetables has to say for itself.
holidays.origin: Started in 1985 by the Farm Animal Rights Movement (FARM) as a way to encourage people to explore plant-based eating on the first day of spring.
holidays.funFact: It is timed to the first day of spring to symbolize fresh starts and new growth, which is why the day is sometimes called a 'spring cleaning for your diet.'

holidays.name: Proposal Day
holidays.description: A day for popping the question, whether it is 'Will you marry me?' or 'Will you share your fries?' Romantics and hopeful daters pick this date to make big moves.
holidays.origin: An informal observance popularized in recent years, it sits within the spring tradition of renewal and new beginnings, and it has been promoted by greeting card and wedding industries.
holidays.funFact: The tradition of the diamond engagement ring dates to 1477, when Archduke Maximilian of Austria reportedly gave one to Mary of Burgundy.

holidays.name: Ravioli Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate little stuffed pillows of pasta, filled with cheese, meat, or veggies. Home cooks and pasta lovers get an excuse to eat dumplings with Italian flair.
holidays.origin: Ravioli is a traditional Italian dish with roots going back to the 14th century, and food-day calendars have marked it on March 20 as an unofficial celebration.
holidays.funFact: In 1930s America, canned ravioli became hugely popular, and the first canned versions were sold by Chef Boyardee, whose founder was an Italian immigrant named Ettore Boiardi.
